blocks.raw:
<LawCallout code="ra9266" section="UAP Doc 301, RA 9184" title="Bidding Procedures Overview">
Three bidding methods: (1) Competitive Bidding — open to all qualified bidders; (2) Negotiated Contract — Owner selects contractor without competitive bidding (for specialized work, time constraints, or established relationships); (3) Invited Bidding — pre-qualified contractors invited without public advertisement. Under RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act), public projects must use competitive bidding with award to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder.
</LawCallout>

blocks.raw:
<ProcessFlow>
  **Competitive Bidding Process:**
  Step 1: Architect prepares bid documents (drawings, specs, instructions to bidders)
  Step 2: Owner advertises project (newspapers, journals, websites)
  Step 3: Pre-bid meeting conducted (typically 1 week before deadline)
  Step 4: Bidders submit sealed bids with bid bond (1-5% of bid amount)
  Step 5: Bids opened publicly (amounts read aloud)
  Step 6: Architect evaluates bids and recommends award
  Step 7: Owner issues Notice of Award to selected bidder
  Step 8: Contractor signs Agreement and posts Performance/Payment Bonds
</ProcessFlow>

blocks.raw:
<ExamTip>
  **LEA Priority — Know the Differences:**
  - **Competitive** = public announcement, multiple bidders, sealed bids, public opening
  - **Negotiated** = single contractor, direct negotiation, no bid bond required typically
  - **Invited** = pre-qualified list, no public ad, still uses sealed bids
  - **Public projects** (RA 9184): must award to lowest responsive, responsible bidder
  - **Private projects**: Owner may consider qualifications, past performance, schedule in addition to price
</ExamTip>

blocks.raw:
<WikiMistakeList
  mistakes={[
    "Assuming the Owner must accept the lowest bid in private projects — in private bidding, the Owner may consider qualifications and other factors",
    "Believing negotiated contracts don't require documentation — cost breakdowns and price justifications are still required",
    "Confusing invited bidding with sole-source procurement — invited bidding still involves multiple pre-qualified bidders",
    "Thinking bid bonds are optional in competitive bidding — bid bonds (1-5%) are required to guarantee the bidder will enter into the contract",
    "Assuming late bids can be accepted with a penalty — bids received after the deadline are rejected even if only slightly late",
  ]}
/>
